readingSections.title: What is a Ratio?
readingSections.content: A ratio compares two or more quantities of the SAME unit by division. It tells you HOW MANY times one quantity contains the other. If there are 2 apples and 3 oranges, the ratio of apples to oranges is 2 : 3. A ratio has NO unit because the units cancel out when one quantity is divided by the other.

subsections.title: Writing a Ratio
subsections.content: The ratio of a to b is written a : b and equals a/b where b is not zero. The two parts are called the antecedent (a) and the consequent (b). Order matters: 2 : 3 is not the same as 3 : 2.

subsections.title: Simplest Form
subsections.content: A ratio is written in its simplest form when both terms are whole numbers with no common factor. Example: 10 : 15 = 2 : 3 (divide both by 5). Always convert to the same units first: 1 m : 50 cm means 100 cm : 50 cm = 2 : 1.

subsections.title: Ratio of More Than Two Quantities
subsections.content: Ratios can involve 3 terms: a : b : c. The simplest form simply divides all three by their common factor. Example: 12 : 18 : 24 = 2 : 3 : 4.

readingSections.title: Types of Ratio
readingSections.content: Based on the powers of the terms, ratios get special names. These appear directly as short questions, so memorizing the names and their formula patterns is worth easy marks.

subsections.title: Duplicate & Sub-duplicate Ratio
subsections.content: Duplicate ratio of a : b is a^2 : b^2. Example: duplicate ratio of 2 : 3 is 4 : 9. Sub-duplicate ratio is the square root of each term, so x : y becomes x(1/2) : y(1/2).

subsections.title: Triplicate & Sub-triplicate Ratio
subsections.content: Triplicate ratio of a : b is a^3 : b^3. Example: triplicate of 2 : 3 is 8 : 27. Sub-triplicate ratio is the cube root, so a : b becomes a(1/3) : b(1/3).

subsections.title: Compound & Inverse Ratio
subsections.content: Compound ratio of (a : x), (b : y), (c : z) is (abc : xyz). Inverse ratio of a : b is b : a. Example: inverse of 5 : 8 is 8 : 5.

readingSections.title: What is a Proportion?
readingSections.content: When two ratios are EQUAL, the four terms are said to be in proportion. a : b = c : d is written as a : b :: c : d and read as 'a is to b as c is to d'. The outer terms (a and d) are the extremes, the inner terms (b and c) are the means.

subsections.title: Product of Means = Product of Extremes
subsections.content: In a proportion a : b = c : d we always have a x d = b x c. This is the single most used rule. Example: check 2 : 3 :: 8 : 12. 2 x 12 = 24 and 3 x 8 = 24, so yes they are proportional.

subsections.title: Checking Proportionality
subsections.content: To check if two ratios are proportional, cross-multiply. 5 : 10 and 1 : 2 are proportional because 5 x 2 = 10 and 10 x 1 = 10. To find an unknown term k in k : 5 = 10 : 25, write k x 25 = 5 x 10, so k = 50/25 = 2.

readingSections.title: Mean, Third & Fourth Proportional
readingSections.content: These three questions appear often: given two numbers, find their mean / third / fourth proportional. Each has a fixed formula, so learn them and the questions take under 10 seconds.

subsections.title: Mean Proportional
subsections.content: The mean proportional between x and y is sqrt(x y). So for a and b it is sqrt(a x b). Example: mean proportional of 4 and 9 is sqrt(36) = 6. Reason: x : m :: m : y means m^2 = x y.

subsections.title: Third Proportional
subsections.content: If p : q = q : s, then s = q^2 / p is the third proportional to p and q. Example: third proportional to 2 and 8 = 8^2 / 2 = 64 / 2 = 32.

subsections.title: Fourth Proportional
subsections.content: If u : v = x : y, then y is the fourth proportional of u, v and x and y = v x / u. Example: fourth proportional to 3, 5 and 6 is (5 x 6) / 3 = 10.

readingSections.title: Direct & Inverse Proportion
readingSections.content: Variation problems relate two quantities with a constant k. When one increases and the other also increases in the same proportion, they are directly proportional. When one increases and the other decreases, they are inversely proportional.

subsections.title: Direct Proportion
subsections.content: a is directly proportional to b (a varies as b) if a/b = k, a constant. If 4 notebooks cost Rs 80, 7 notebooks at the same rate cost 140. Because cost/no of notebooks is constant.

subsections.title: Inverse Proportion
subsections.content: a is inversely proportional to b if a x b = k. More workers means fewer days: if 6 workers build in 12 days, 12 workers build in 6 days. Because workers x days is constant.

subsections.title: Spotting the Type
subsections.content: Ask: 'if x grows, does y grow (direct) or shrink (inverse)?' Speed and time are inverse, distance and time are direct, workers and days are inverse, items and cost are direct.

readingSections.title: Dividing a Quantity in a Given Ratio
readingSections.content: A very common problem: split an amount Rs X in the ratio a : b. The total has (a + b) parts, each part is X / (a + b), the first share is a parts and the second b parts. This one type covers a huge exam share.

subsections.title: The Formula
subsections.content: To divide X in ratio a : b, first = aX / (a+b), second = bX / (a+b). Example: divide Rs 981 in 5 : 4. Sum is 9, one part = 981/9 = 109, so 5 x 109 = 545 and 4 x 109 = 436.

subsections.title: Sharing between three people
subsections.content: For a : b : c, sum = a + b + c, and shares are aX/(a+b+c), bX/(a+b+c), cX/(a+b+c). Example: 500 in 2 : 3 : 5 gives 100, 150, 250.

readingSections.title: Combining Ratios (found a : c)
readingSections.content: When two ratios share a common term, we combine them by making the common term equal. If a : b = 2 : 3 and b : c = 5 : 7, we make b equal in both using the LCM of the two b-values, then read a : b : c directly.

subsections.title: Step-by-Step Combining
subsections.content: Make b equal: b is 3 in the first and 5 in the second. LCM(3,5) = 15. Multiply first ratio parts by 5: a : b = 10 : 15. Multiply second by 3: b : c = 15 : 21. Now a : b : c = 10 : 15 : 21, so a : c = 10 : 21.

subsections.title: Three-Ratio Chain
subsections.content: For a:b = p:x, b:c = q:y, c:d = r:z, extend by multiplying in sequence to get a : b : c : d = p q r : x q r : x y r : x y z.

readingSections.title: Coins and Denominations
readingSections.content: Here a bag has coins of different values (say 50p, 25p, 1 rupee) in a given ratio, and you must find the number of coins. The trick: the ratio given is a RATIO OF VALUES, so convert each value to a count by dividing by the coin value, or convert counts to value by multiplying.

subsections.title: Ratio of Values to Number of Coins
subsections.content: If values of 50p, 25p, 10p coins are in ratio V1 : V2 : V3, then the number of coins are (V1/0.5) : (V2/0.25) : (V3/0.1). Example: values 11 : 9 : 5 for 1, 0.5, 0.25 rupee coins -> counts 11 : 18 : 20.

subsections.title: Counting the Total Value
subsections.content: If the number of coins is in ratio c1 : c2 : c3 and values are v1, v2, v3, total value = c1v1 x k + c2v2 x k + c3v3 x k. Equate to given total, solve k, then multiply back.

readingSections.title: Mixture & Alligation with Ratios
readingSections.content: A mixture problem gives two substances in a ratio, then adds or removes a part of one substance, and asks for the new ratio. Key idea: the quantity of the UNCHANGED component stays constant; only the changed component responds.

subsections.title: Adding a Component
subsections.content: Alcohol and water in 7 : 5; add 8 litres of water, new ratio 7 : 9. Let quantities be 7k and 5k. Since only water changed: 7k / (5k + 8) = 7 / 9 -> 63k = 35k + 56 -> 28k = 56 -> k = 2. Alcohol = 14 litres.

subsections.title: Removing then Adding
subsections.content: If a fixed amount of a mixture is removed and replaced by pure milk, first compute what remains of each component in the leftover and then add the pure milk. Only the milk value goes up by the added amount.

readingSections.title: Income, Expenditure & Salary Ratio
readingSections.content: These problems give the income ratio of two people, plus savings or expenditure ratios, and ask for income. The core identity is: Income - Expenditure = Savings. Translate each given ratio into one equation, then solve.

subsections.title: The Identity to Remember
subsections.content: For each person: Income - Expenditure = Saving. If their incomes are in ratio 4 : 5 and their savings are Rs 4000 : Rs 5000, set incomes as 4x, 5x and solve for x via the common difference.

subsections.title: Expenditure Ratio
subsections.content: When income and expenditure ratios are given, pick income = ax + e and expenditure = by + e, then saving = (a - b)x. Matching the saving ratio gives one equation for x and one unknown.

readingSections.title: Partnership & Profit Sharing
readingSections.content: When money is invested in a business and profit is shared, profit is divided in the ratio of (Capital x Time). If all invest the same time, profit is simply the ratio of capitals. This is marriage of proportion with multiplication.

subsections.title: Same Term, Profit = Capital Ratio
subsections.content: A invests 100 and B invests 200 for the same period, profit 30000 is split in 1 : 2 -> A gets 10000, B gets 20000. Reason: profit stays in the ratio of capital when time is identical.

subsections.title: Different Time, Profit = Capital x Time
subsections.content: If capital changes after some months, compute each partner's input as sum of (amount x months) for each time segment, then divide profit in the ratio of those inputs. Example: A 10000 x 5 + 7000 x 7 = 99000.

formulas.title: Basic Ratio and its Simplest Form

formula.text: Ratio of a to b is a divided by b.

formulas.whenToUse: Comparing any two quantities of the same unit (length, money, speed, marks).
explanation: The ratio a : b is the same as the fraction a/b.
To simplify, divide both terms by their highest common factor (HCF).
Convert both quantities to the same unit before comparing.

example.prompt: Find the ratio between 12 m and 800 cm.
steps: Convert 12 m to cm if you will divide: 12 m = 1200 cm.

formulas.memoryTip: Ratio has no unit because the units cancel out.
formulas.commonMistake: Comparing different units without converting, e.g. 12 m : 80 cm directly.

formulas.title: Duplicate, Sub-duplicate, Triplicate, Compound & Inverse

formula.latex: \text{dup} = a^2 : b^2 \quad \text{tri} = a^3 : b^3 \\\text{inverse} = b : a \quad \text{compound} = (a x)(b y) ...
formula.text: Square for duplicate, cube for triplicate, swap for inverse.

explanation: Duplicate ratio of a : b is a^2 : b^2.
Triplicate ratio is a^3 : b^3.
Compound ratio of a : x and b : y is (a x : b y).
Inverse ratio of a : b is b : a.

example.prompt: Find the duplicate and triplicate ratios of 2 : 3.

formulas.memoryTip: Duplicate = square, sub-duplicate = root, triplicate = cube, sub-triplicate = cube root.
formulas.commonMistake: Adding terms instead of multiplying / powering them.

formulas.title: Proportion — Product of Means

formula.latex: a : b = c : d \Rightarrow a \times d = b \times c
formula.text: For a proportion, product of extremes equals product of means.

formulas.whenToUse: Checking proportionality or finding a missing term in a proportion.
explanation: In a : b :: c : d, extremes are a and d, means are b and c.
Extremes product equals means product: a d = b c.
To check, cross-multiply both sides.

example.prompt: Check if 2 : 6 and 8 : 12 are in proportion.
steps: 24 is not equal to 48, so NOT proportional.

formulas.memoryTip: Extremes times extremes = means times means.
formulas.commonMistake: Checking equality after simplifying both ratios but overlooking sign.

formulas.title: Mean, Third & Fourth Proportional

formula.text: Three formulas: sqrt of product for mean, q-square over p for third, v times x over u for fourth.

explanation: Mean proportional between x and y is sqrt(x y).
Third proportional to p, q is q^2 / p.
Fourth proportional to u, v, x is (v x) / u.

example.prompt: Find the third proportional to 2 and 8.
steps: Let the third be s. Then 2 : 8 = 8 : s.

formulas.memoryTip: Mean = route of product; third = square over first; fourth = branch over first.
formulas.commonMistake: Swapping which term is the square.

formulas.title: Dividing a Quantity in the Ratio a : b

formula.text: Split X into two shares proportional to a and b.

explanation: Sum of ratio terms a + b gives total parts.
Each part = X / (a + b).
First share = a parts, second = b parts.
For three people use a + b + c in place of a + b.

example.prompt: John and Mark share Rs 500 in 3 : 2.

formulas.memoryTip: Find one share, the other is the total minus it.
formulas.commonMistake: Multiplying the whole amount by the ratio instead of the parts.

formulas.title: Combined Ratio a : b : c

formula.latex: a:b = x:y,\ b:c = p:q \Rightarrow a:b:c = xp : yp : yq
formula.text: Make the middle term b equal using its two given values.

formulas.whenToUse: When two part : find a : c or a : b : c from two overlapping ratios.
explanation: Take b-term values y from second and p case from the second ratio.
Multiply the two ratio terms by factors coming from the OTHER ratio.
Multiply the first ratio by the second ratio's b-term and vice versa.
Align the b terms to be equal, aggregate the result.

example.prompt: a : b = 2 : 3 and b : c = 5 : 7, find a : c.
steps: b is 3 in the first and 5 in the second; LCM(3,5) = 15.
First becomes a : b = 10 : 15, second b : c = 15 : 21.

formulas.memoryTip: The middle term is the bridge: make it n images. equal.

formulas.title: Profit = Capital x Time

formula.latex: \text{Profit ratio} = C_1 T_1 : C_2 T_2 : C_3 T_3
formula.text: For each partner, multiply their capital by how many months.

explanation: One partner same for all, profit splits by capital ratio.
If capitals change mid-year, sum segments: 6 months x 10000 + 6 months x 12000.
The result ratio is the ratio of the shares in profit.

example.prompt: A invests Rs 1000 for 6 months, B invests Rs 2000 for 3 months. Profit Rs 3000.

formulas.memoryTip: Lower capital? Longer time compensates and still equal.
formulas.commonMistake: Ignoring the time factor, dividing profit purely by capital.

formulas.title: Coins: Value to Count

formula.text: Value ratio divided by the rupee value of each coin gives the count.

explanation: Number of coins = Value of that type / value per coin.
If value of Rs1, 50p, 25p coins are in ratio 11 : 2 : 1.
Verify sum of counts agrees with total told in the question.

example.prompt: Coins in a purse have 1 Rs, 50p, 25p with values in ratio 11 : 25. There are 342 coins total.

formulas.memoryTip: Divide value by coin size, then use total to fix the multiplier.
formulas.commonMistake: Treating the value ratio directly as a count ratio.

formulas.title: Direct & Inverse Proportion

formula.text: Direct: ratio stays, complete the cross-multiplication. Inverse: product stays.

explanation: If y is directly proportional to x, then x1/y1 = x2/y2.
If y is inversely proportional, the product x x y is constant.
Identify by asking 'more of x -> more of y (direct) or less (inverse)?'

example.prompt: 6 men make a wall in 10 days. In how many days will 15 men make it?

formulas.commonMistake: Applying direct while the quantities actually vary inversely.

formulas.title: Salary Ratio after Equal Increase

formula.text: If both add the same amount, other cross-multiply.

explanation: Let original incomes be a x and b x.
Adding k to both gives new ratio m : n.
Cross-multiply and solve for x.
Verify the number asked, e.g. the second salary = b x + k.

example.prompt: Incomes of Ram & Sham are 4 : 5. After +5000 each the ratio is 50 : 60. Now Sham's income?
steps: Sham's original = 5x = 25000, then the +5000 became: sham's current 30000.

formulas.memoryTip: Increase the same amount, the bigger original stays bigger.
formulas.commonMistake: Finding the old salary when the question asks the new one.

mcqs.q: Find the ratio between 12 m and 800 cm.
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Convert 12 m to cm. 12 m = 1200 cm. Step 2: Ratio = 1200 : 800. Step 3: Divide both terms by 400. Ratio = 3 : 2. Answer is option B.

mcqs.q: Simplify the ratio 45 : 75.
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Find the HCF of 45 and 75, which is 15. Step 2: 45 ÷ 15 = 3 and 75 ÷ 15 = 5. Step 3: Simplified ratio = 3 : 5. Answer is option A.

mcqs.q: Find the ratio of 1.5 to 0.75.
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Multiply both terms by 100 to remove decimals: 150 : 75. Step 2: Divide both by 75. Ratio = 2 : 1. Answer is option B.

mcqs.q: If a : b = 2 : 3 and a = 40, find b.
mcqs.exp: Step 1: a : b = 2 : 3 means a/b = 2/3. Step 2: 40/b = 2/3. Step 3: Cross-multiply: 2b = 120, so b = 60. Answer is option C.

mcqs.q: 4 notebooks cost Rs 80. How much will 7 notebooks cost?
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Cost of 1 notebook = 80 ÷ 4 = Rs 20. Step 2: Cost of 7 notebooks = 7 × 20 = Rs 140. Answer is option C.

mcqs.q: If x : y = 3 : 4 and x + y = 28, find x.
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Let x = 3k and y = 4k. Step 2: 3k + 4k = 28, so 7k = 28 and k = 4. Step 3: x = 3 × 4 = 12. Answer is option B.

mcqs.q: Reduce 60 paise to Rs 3 to its simplest ratio.
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Convert Rs 3 to paise = 300 paise. Step 2: Ratio = 60 : 300. Step 3: Divide both by 60, ratio = 1 : 5. Answer is option A.

mcqs.q: Two numbers are in the ratio 4 : 7 and their difference is 24. Find the numbers.
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Let the numbers be 4k and 7k. Step 2: 7k − 4k = 3k = 24, so k = 8. Step 3: Numbers = 4 × 8 = 32 and 7 × 8 = 56. Answer is option C.

mcqs.q: Simplify the ratio 1/2 : 1/3.
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Multiply both fractions by the LCM of denominators, 6. Step 2: (1/2 × 6) : (1/3 × 6) = 3 : 2. Answer is option B.

mcqs.q: If a : b = 5 : 6 and b = 18, find a.
mcqs.exp: Step 1: a/b = 5/6. Step 2: a/18 = 5/6. Step 3: Cross-multiply: 6a = 90, so a = 15. Answer is option B.

mcqs.q: The angles of a triangle are in the ratio 1 : 2 : 3. Find the largest angle.
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Let angles be k, 2k, 3k. Sum = 6k = 180°, so k = 30°. Step 2: Largest angle = 3k = 90°. Answer is option B.

mcqs.q: Divide 84 in the ratio 5 : 7.
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Total parts = 5 + 7 = 12. Step 2: Each part = 84 ÷ 12 = 7. Step 3: Parts = 5 × 7 = 35 and 7 × 7 = 49. Answer is option B.

mcqs.q: Simplify 12 : 18 : 24.
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Find the HCF of 12, 18 and 24, which is 6. Step 2: Divide each term by 6: 2 : 3 : 4. Answer is option A.

mcqs.q: If a : b = 7 : 9 and a + b = 64, find b.
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Let a = 7k, b = 9k. Sum = 16k = 64, so k = 4. Step 2: b = 9 × 4 = 36. Answer is option C.

mcqs.q: The ratio of speeds of two cars is 60 km/h : 80 km/h. Simplify it.
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Ratio = 60 : 80. Step 2: Divide both by 20. Ratio = 3 : 4. Answer is option B.

mcqs.q: A sum of Rs 250 is split such that A gets 2/5 of it. What does A get?
mcqs.exp: Step 1: A's share = (2/5) × 250. Step 2: 250 ÷ 5 = 50, then 50 × 2 = Rs 100. Answer is option C.

mcqs.q: Find the ratio of 25 minutes to 1 hour 40 minutes.
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Convert 1 hr 40 min = 100 minutes. Step 2: Ratio = 25 : 100 = 1 : 4. Answer is option A.

mcqs.q: If x : y = 3 : 5 and x + y = 56, find y.
mcqs.exp: Step 1: x = 3k, y = 5k. Sum = 8k = 56, so k = 7. Step 2: y = 5 × 7 = 35. Answer is option C.

mcqs.q: Express 3 : 5 as a fraction and as a percentage.
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Ratio 3 : 5 is the fraction 3/5. Step 2: Percentage = (3/5) × 100 = 60%. Answer is option A.

mcqs.q: Two numbers are in the ratio 2 : 3. If 8 is added to each, the new numbers are in the ratio 3 : 4. Find the smaller number.
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Let numbers be 2k and 3k. Step 2: (2k+8)/(3k+8) = 3/4. Step 3: 4(2k+8) = 3(3k+8), so 8k+32 = 9k+24, giving k = 8. Step 4: Smaller number = 2 × 8 = 16. Answer is option B.

mcqs.q: Find the duplicate ratio of 3 : 5.
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Duplicate ratio means squaring both terms. Step 2: 3² : 5² = 9 : 25. Answer is option B.

mcqs.q: Find the sub-duplicate ratio of 16 : 25.
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Sub-duplicate ratio means taking the square root of both terms. Step 2: √16 : √25 = 4 : 5. Answer is option A.

mcqs.q: Find the triplicate ratio of 2 : 3.
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Triplicate ratio means cubing both terms. Step 2: 2³ : 3³ = 8 : 27. Answer is option B.

mcqs.q: Find the sub-triplicate ratio of 27 : 64.
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Sub-triplicate means taking the cube root of both terms. Step 2: ³√27 : ³√64 = 3 : 4. Answer is option B.

mcqs.q: Find the inverse ratio of 7 : 9.
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Inverse ratio is obtained by swapping the terms. Step 2: Inverse of 7 : 9 = 9 : 7. Answer is option B.

mcqs.q: Find the compound ratio of (2 : 3), (4 : 5) and (6 : 7).
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Multiply the first terms: 2 × 4 × 6 = 48. Step 2: Multiply the second terms: 3 × 5 × 7 = 105. Step 3: Compound ratio = 48 : 105. Step 4: Divide both by 3, ratio = 16 : 35. Answer is option A.

mcqs.q: The duplicate ratio of 5 : 6 is:
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Square both terms. Step 2: 5² : 6² = 25 : 36. Answer is option A.

mcqs.q: The sub-duplicate ratio of 9 : 16 is:
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Take the square root of each term. Step 2: √9 : √16 = 3 : 4. Answer is option B.

mcqs.q: Find the triplicate ratio of 1 : 2.
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Cube both terms. Step 2: 1³ : 2³ = 1 : 8. Answer is option B.

mcqs.q: Find the compound ratio of (5 : 6) and (8 : 9).
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Multiply first terms: 5 × 8 = 40. Step 2: Multiply second terms: 6 × 9 = 54. Step 3: Ratio = 40 : 54. Step 4: Divide both by 2, ratio = 20 : 27. Answer is option B.

mcqs.q: Find the duplicate of the inverse of 2 : 3.
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Inverse of 2 : 3 = 3 : 2. Step 2: Duplicate means squaring: 3² : 2² = 9 : 4. Answer is option B.

mcqs.q: The ratio of the squares of 4 and 9 is called the ___ of 4 : 9.
mcqs.exp: Step 1: The ratio of squares of two numbers is called the duplicate ratio. Step 2: Here it is 16 : 81. Answer is option B.

mcqs.q: Find x if x : 5 = 10 : 25.
mcqs.exp: Step 1: In a proportion, product of extremes = product of means. Step 2: x × 25 = 5 × 10 = 50. Step 3: x = 50/25 = 2. Answer is option B.

mcqs.q: Are 3 : 5 and 9 : 15 in proportion?
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Check 3 × 15 = 45 and 5 × 9 = 45. Step 2: Products are equal, so yes, they are in proportion. Answer is option A.

mcqs.q: Find x if 4 : 9 = 12 : x.
mcqs.exp: Step 1: 4/9 = 12/x. Step 2: Cross-multiply: 4x = 9 × 12 = 108. Step 3: x = 108/4 = 27. Answer is option B.

mcqs.q: Which pair is in proportion: 2 : 4 :: ?
mcqs.exp: Step 1: 2 : 4 simplifies to 1 : 2. Step 2: Check options: 5 : 10 also simplifies to 1 : 2. Step 3: So 2 : 4 :: 5 : 10. Answer is option B.

mcqs.q: Find x if x : 6 = 8 : 12.
mcqs.exp: Step 1: x/6 = 8/12. Step 2: Simplify 8/12 = 2/3. Step 3: x = 6 × (2/3) = 4. Answer is option B.

mcqs.q: Are 5 : 8 and 10 : 16 in proportion?
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Check 5 × 16 = 80 and 8 × 10 = 80. Step 2: Products are equal, so yes. Answer is option A.

mcqs.q: Find x if 7 : 14 = x : 8.
mcqs.exp: Step 1: 7/14 = x/8, simplify 7/14 = 1/2. Step 2: x = 8 × (1/2) = 4. Answer is option C.

mcqs.q: Check if 3 : 5 :: 12 : 20 holds.
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Check extremes: 3 × 20 = 60. Step 2: Check means: 5 × 12 = 60. Step 3: Equal, so yes. Answer is option A.

mcqs.q: Find x if 3 : 7 = 9 : x.
mcqs.exp: Step 1: 3/7 = 9/x. Step 2: Cross-multiply: 3x = 63. Step 3: x = 63/3 = 21. Answer is option B.

mcqs.q: Find x if 2 : 3 = x : 18.
mcqs.exp: Step 1: 2/3 = x/18. Step 2: Cross-multiply: 3x = 36. Step 3: x = 12. Answer is option C.

mcqs.q: Find the mean proportional between 4 and 9.
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Mean proportional = √(a × b). Step 2: √(4 × 9) = √36 = 6. Answer is option B.

mcqs.q: Find the third proportional to 4 and 12.
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Third proportional s satisfies 4 : 12 = 12 : s. Step 2: 4s = 12 × 12 = 144. Step 3: s = 144/4 = 36. Answer is option C.

mcqs.q: Find the fourth proportional to 3, 5 and 6.
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Let it be y: 3 : 5 = 6 : y. Step 2: 3y = 5 × 6 = 30. Step 3: y = 30/3 = 10. Answer is option B.

mcqs.q: Find the mean proportional between 8 and 18.
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Mean proportional = √(a × b) = √(8 × 18). Step 2: √144 = 12. Answer is option B.

mcqs.exp: Step 1: Third proportional s satisfies 2 : 8 = 8 : s. Step 2: 2s = 64. Step 3: s = 32. Answer is option C.

mcqs.q: Find the fourth proportional to 2, 3 and 8.
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Let it be y: 2 : 3 = 8 : y. Step 2: 2y = 3 × 8 = 24. Step 3: y = 12. Answer is option B.

mcqs.q: Find the mean proportional between 0.5 and 2.
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Mean proportional = √(0.5 × 2) = √1. Step 2: = 1. Answer is option B.

mcqs.q: Find the third proportional to 9 and 15.
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Third proportional s: 9 : 15 = 15 : s. Step 2: 9s = 225. Step 3: s = 25. Answer is option C.

mcqs.q: Find the fourth proportional to 5, 6 and 10.
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Let it be y: 5 : 6 = 10 : y. Step 2: 5y = 6 × 10 = 60. Step 3: y = 60/5 = 12. Answer is option C.

mcqs.q: The mean proportional between two numbers is 12 and their product is 144. The numbers are:
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Mean proportional m satisfies m² = a × b. Step 2: 12² = 144 = a × b. Step 3: Among options, 9 × 16 = 144. Answer is option B.

mcqs.q: Divide Rs 981 in the ratio 5 : 4.
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Total parts = 5 + 4 = 9. Step 2: One part = 981/9 = 109. Step 3: Shares = 5 × 109 = 545 and 4 × 109 = 436. Answer is option A.

mcqs.q: Divide Rs 1040 in the ratio 5 : 8.
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Total parts = 13. Step 2: One part = 1040/13 = 80. Step 3: Shares = 5 × 80 = 400 and 8 × 80 = 640. Answer is option A.

mcqs.q: Divide Rs 300 among A, B, C in the ratio 1 : 2 : 3.
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Total parts = 1 + 2 + 3 = 6. Step 2: One part = 300/6 = 50. Step 3: Shares = 50, 100, 150. Answer is option B.

mcqs.q: Divide Rs 600 in the ratio 2 : 3.
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Total parts = 5. Step 2: One part = 600/5 = 120. Step 3: Shares = 2 × 120 = 240 and 3 × 120 = 360. Answer is option B.

mcqs.q: Divide 100 into two parts proportional to 3 : 5.
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Total parts = 8. Step 2: One part = 100/8 = 12.5. Step 3: Shares = 3 × 12.5 = 37.5 and 5 × 12.5 = 62.5. Answer is option A.

mcqs.q: A and B share Rs 900 in the ratio 4 : 5. What is A's share?
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Total parts = 9. Step 2: One part = 900/9 = 100. Step 3: A's share = 4 × 100 = Rs 400. Answer is option A.

mcqs.q: Divide Rs 72 in the ratio 5 : 3.
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Total parts = 8. Step 2: One part = 72/8 = 9. Step 3: Shares = 5 × 9 = 45 and 3 × 9 = 27. Answer is option B.

mcqs.q: Divide Rs 8000 in the ratio 3 : 5.
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Total parts = 8. Step 2: One part = 8000/8 = 1000. Step 3: Shares = 3 × 1000 = 3000 and 5 × 1000 = 5000. Answer is option A.

mcqs.q: Divide Rs 240 in the ratio 7 : 5.
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Total parts = 12. Step 2: One part = 240/12 = 20. Step 3: Shares = 7 × 20 = 140 and 5 × 20 = 100. Answer is option B.

mcqs.q: Divide Rs 4500 in the ratio 2 : 3 : 4.
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Total parts = 9. Step 2: One part = 4500/9 = 500. Step 3: Shares = 2 × 500 = 1000, 3 × 500 = 1500, 4 × 500 = 2000. Answer is option B.

mcqs.q: Divide Rs 360 in the ratio 5 : 7.
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Total parts = 12. Step 2: One part = 360/12 = 30. Step 3: Shares = 5 × 30 = 150 and 7 × 30 = 210. Answer is option A.

mcqs.q: Two parts of 88 are in the ratio 3 : 5. Find the parts.
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Total parts = 8. Step 2: One part = 88/8 = 11. Step 3: Parts = 3 × 11 = 33 and 5 × 11 = 55. Answer is option B.

mcqs.q: Rs 1500 is divided among A, B, C in 2 : 3 : 5. Find B's share.
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Total parts = 10. Step 2: One part = 1500/10 = 150. Step 3: B's share = 3 × 150 = Rs 450. Answer is option C.

mcqs.q: Divide Rs 120 in the ratio 1 : 2 : 3.
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Total parts = 6. Step 2: One part = 120/6 = 20. Step 3: Shares = 20, 40, 60. Answer is option A.

mcqs.q: Two numbers are in the ratio 2 : 3 and their sum is 60. Find the numbers.
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Total parts = 5. Step 2: One part = 60/5 = 12. Step 3: Numbers = 2 × 12 = 24 and 3 × 12 = 36. Answer is option B.

mcqs.q: Divide Rs 540 in the ratio 4 : 5.
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Total parts = 9. Step 2: One part = 540/9 = 60. Step 3: Shares = 4 × 60 = 240 and 5 × 60 = 300. Answer is option A.

mcqs.q: Divide Rs 720 in the ratio 7 : 9.
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Total parts = 16. Step 2: One part = 720/16 = 45. Step 3: Shares = 7 × 45 = 315 and 9 × 45 = 405. Answer is option B.

mcqs.q: Rs 900 is divided in the ratio 3 : 4 : 5. What is the middle share?
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Total parts = 12. Step 2: One part = 900/12 = 75. Step 3: Middle share = 4 × 75 = Rs 300. Answer is option B.

mcqs.q: Divide Rs 60 in the ratio 2 : 3 : 5.
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Total parts = 10. Step 2: One part = 60/10 = 6. Step 3: Shares = 2 × 6 = 12, 3 × 6 = 18, 5 × 6 = 30. Answer is option A.

mcqs.q: A sum of money is divided between P and Q in 3 : 2. P gets Rs 270. Find the total sum.
mcqs.exp: Step 1: P gets 3 parts = 270, so 1 part = 90. Step 2: Total parts = 5, so total = 5 × 90 = Rs 450. Answer is option C.

mcqs.q: If a : b = 2 : 3 and b : c = 4 : 5, find a : b : c.
mcqs.exp: Step 1: b is 3 in the first and 4 in the second; LCM(3,4) = 12. Step 2: a : b = 8 : 12 and b : c = 12 : 15. Step 3: a : b : c = 8 : 12 : 15. Answer is option A.

mcqs.q: If a : b = 3 : 4 and b : c = 6 : 7, find a : b : c.
mcqs.exp: Step 1: LCM(4,6) = 12. Step 2: a : b = 9 : 12 and b : c = 12 : 14. Step 3: a : b : c = 9 : 12 : 14. Answer is option A.

mcqs.q: If a : b = 1 : 2 and b : c = 2 : 3, find a : b : c.
mcqs.exp: Step 1: b already matches: b = 2 in both. Step 2: a : b : c = 1 : 2 : 3. Answer is option A.

mcqs.q: If a : b = 5 : 7 and b : c = 8 : 9, find a : b : c.
mcqs.exp: Step 1: LCM(7,8) = 56. Step 2: a : b = 40 : 56 and b : c = 56 : 63. Step 3: a : b : c = 40 : 56 : 63. Answer is option A.

mcqs.q: If a : b = 2 : 3 and b : c = 4 : 9, find a : b : c.
mcqs.exp: Step 1: LCM(3,4) = 12. Step 2: a : b = 8 : 12 and b : c = 12 : 27. Step 3: a : b : c = 8 : 12 : 27. Answer is option A.

mcqs.q: If a : b : c = 4 : 5 : 6, find a : b and b : c.
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Read the combined ratio directly. Step 2: a : b = 4 : 5 and b : c = 5 : 6. Answer is option A.

mcqs.q: If a : b = 3 : 5 and b : c = 5 : 7, find a : c.
mcqs.exp: Step 1: b is 5 in both ratios. Step 2: a : b : c = 3 : 5 : 7. Step 3: a : c = 3 : 7. Answer is option A.

mcqs.q: If a : b = 2 : 3 and b : c = 3 : 4, find a : c.
mcqs.exp: Step 1: b = 3 in both ratios. Step 2: a : b : c = 2 : 3 : 4. Step 3: a : c = 2 : 4 = 1 : 2. Answer is option A.

mcqs.q: If a : b = 6 : 7 and b : c = 14 : 15, find a : c.
mcqs.exp: Step 1: LCM(7,14) = 14. Step 2: a : b = 12 : 14 and b : c = 14 : 15. Step 3: a : c = 12 : 15 = 4 : 5. Answer is option A.

mcqs.q: If x : y = 4 : 5 and y : z = 10 : 13, find x : z.
mcqs.exp: Step 1: LCM(5,10) = 10. Step 2: x : y = 8 : 10 and y : z = 10 : 13. Step 3: x : z = 8 : 13. Answer is option A.

mcqs.q: If a : b = 7 : 9 and b : c = 6 : 11, find a : b : c.
mcqs.exp: Step 1: LCM(9,6) = 18. Step 2: a : b = 14 : 18 and b : c = 18 : 33. Step 3: a : b : c = 14 : 18 : 33. Answer is option B.

mcqs.q: If a : b = 3 : 4 and b : c = 5 : 6, find a : b : c.
mcqs.exp: Step 1: LCM(4,5) = 20. Step 2: a : b = 15 : 20 and b : c = 20 : 24. Step 3: a : b : c = 15 : 20 : 24. Answer is option A.

mcqs.q: If a : b = 2 : 3 and b : c = 9 : 10, find a : b : c.
mcqs.exp: Step 1: LCM(3,9) = 9. Step 2: a : b = 6 : 9 and b : c = 9 : 10. Step 3: a : b : c = 6 : 9 : 10. Answer is option A.

mcqs.q: If a : b = 4 : 9 and b : c = 3 : 5, find a : b : c.
mcqs.exp: Step 1: LCM(9,3) = 9. Step 2: a : b = 4 : 9 and b : c = 9 : 15. Step 3: a : b : c = 4 : 9 : 15. Answer is option B.

mcqs.q: If a : b = 5 : 6 and b : c = 4 : 7, find a : b : c.
mcqs.exp: Step 1: LCM(6,4) = 12. Step 2: a : b = 10 : 12 and b : c = 12 : 21. Step 3: a : b : c = 10 : 12 : 21. Answer is option A.

mcqs.q: If a : b : c = 3 : 4 : 5 and a + c = 40, find b.
mcqs.exp: Step 1: a = 3k, c = 5k, so a + c = 8k = 40, giving k = 5. Step 2: b = 4k = 4 × 5 = 20. Answer is option C.

mcqs.q: If a : b = 8 : 15 and b : c = 5 : 8, find a : c.
mcqs.exp: Step 1: LCM(15,5) = 15. Step 2: a : b = 8 : 15 and b : c = 15 : 24. Step 3: a : c = 8 : 24 = 1 : 3. Answer is option A.

mcqs.q: If A : B = 2 : 3, B : C = 4 : 5, C : D = 6 : 7, find A : D.
mcqs.exp: Step 1: LCM(3,4,6) = 12. Step 2: A : B = 8 : 12, B : C = 12 : 15, C : D = 15 : 17.5 — instead scale directly: A=2×4×6=48 units, D=3×5×7=105. Step 3: A : D = 48 : 105 = 16 : 35. Answer is option A.

mcqs.q: A bag contains 50p, 25p and 10p coins in the ratio 2 : 5 : 3, amounting to Rs 510. Find the number of 50p coins.
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Let counts be 2k, 5k, 3k. Step 2: Value = 0.5×2k + 0.25×5k + 0.1×3k = k + 1.25k + 0.3k = 2.55k. Step 3: 2.55k = 510, so k = 200. Step 4: 50p coins = 2k = 400. Answer is option B.

mcqs.q: A bag contains an equal number of 25p, 50p and 1 rupee coins. The total value is Rs 105. How many coins of each type?
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Let the equal count be k. Step 2: Value = 0.25k + 0.5k + 1k = 1.75k = 105. Step 3: k = 105/1.75 = 60. Answer is option C.

mcqs.q: The values of 50p and 25p coins in a purse are in the ratio 2 : 3. Find the ratio of their counts.
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Count = value ÷ coin size. Step 2: Counts = (2/0.5) : (3/0.25) = 4 : 12. Step 3: Simplify = 1 : 3. Answer is option C.

mcqs.q: A purse has 1 rupee, 50p and 25p coins whose VALUES are in the ratio 11 : 9 : 5. The total number of coins is 490. Find the number of 50p coins.
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Counts = 11 : (9/0.5) : (5/0.25) = 11 : 18 : 20. Step 2: Total units = 49 = 490, so 1 unit = 10. Step 3: 50p coins = 18 × 10 = 180. Answer is option C.

mcqs.q: A purse has 25p and 50p coins in the ratio 3 : 4 by count. Total value is Rs 55. Find the number of 25p coins.
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Let counts be 3k and 4k. Step 2: Value = 0.25×3k + 0.5×4k = 0.75k + 2k = 2.75k = 55. Step 3: k = 20. Step 4: 25p coins = 3 × 20 = 60. Answer is option C.

mcqs.q: 10p, 25p and 50p coins are in the ratio 5 : 4 : 3 by count. Total value is Rs 45. Find the number of 50p coins.
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Counts 5k, 4k, 3k. Step 2: Value = 0.1×5k + 0.25×4k + 0.5×3k = 0.5k + 1k + 1.5k = 3k = 45. Step 3: k = 15. Step 4: 50p coins = 3 × 15 = 45. Answer is option B.

mcqs.q: A bag has 1 rupee and 50p coins, 500 coins in all, total value Rs 300. Find the number of 50p coins.
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Let x be 1 rupee coins, y be 50p coins. x + y = 500. Step 2: Value: x + 0.5y = 300. Step 3: Subtract: 0.5y = 200, so y = 400. Answer is option C.

mcqs.q: 25p and 1 rupee coins are in the ratio 4 : 3 by count. Total value is Rs 100. Find the number of 1 rupee coins.
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Counts 4k and 3k. Step 2: Value = 0.25×4k + 1×3k = k + 3k = 4k = 100. Step 3: k = 25. Step 4: 1 rupee coins = 3 × 25 = 75. Answer is option B.

mcqs.q: 50p, 25p and 10p coins are in the ratio 3 : 4 : 5 by count. Total value is Rs 120. Find the number of 25p coins.
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Counts 3k, 4k, 5k. Step 2: Value = 0.5×3k + 0.25×4k + 0.1×5k = 1.5k + k + 0.5k = 3k = 120. Step 3: k = 40. Step 4: 25p coins = 4 × 40 = 160. Answer is option B.

mcqs.q: The values of 1 rupee, 50p and 25p coins are in the ratio 2 : 3 : 4. Find the ratio of their counts.
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Counts = (2/1) : (3/0.5) : (4/0.25). Step 2: = 2 : 6 : 16. Answer is option A.

mcqs.q: A bag has coins of Rs 1, 50p and 25p in the ratio 1 : 2 : 4 by count. Total value is Rs 120. Find the number of 25p coins.
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Counts k, 2k, 4k. Step 2: Value = 1×k + 0.5×2k + 0.25×4k = k + k + k = 3k = 120. Step 3: k = 40. Step 4: 25p coins = 4 × 40 = 160. Answer is option C.

mcqs.q: Coins of 50p and 25p are in the ratio 1 : 3 by value. If there are 200 coins of 50p, how many 25p coins are there?
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Counts = (1/0.5) : (3/0.25) = 2 : 12 = 1 : 6. Step 2: For 200 50p coins (1 unit), 25p coins = 6 × 200 = 1200? No — 1 unit = 200, so 6 units = 1200. Recheck: ratio counts 2:12 means for every 2 50p coins there are 12 25p coins. 200 50p coins = 100 × 2, so 25p = 100 × 12 = 1200. Answer is option D.

mcqs.q: In a 13-litre mixture, milk : water = 3 : 2. If 3 litres is replaced by 3 litres of milk, find the new ratio.
mcqs.exp: Step 1: After removing 3 L, 10 L of mixture (3:2) remains: milk = 6 L, water = 4 L. Step 2: Add 3 L milk: milk = 9 L, water = 4 L. Step 3: New ratio = 9 : 4. Answer is option B.

mcqs.q: A mixture has alcohol and water in 7 : 5. Adding 8 litres of water makes it 7 : 9. Find the quantity of alcohol.
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Let alcohol = 7k, water = 5k. Step 2: 7k/(5k+8) = 7/9. Step 3: 63k = 35k + 56, so 28k = 56 and k = 2. Step 4: Alcohol = 7 × 2 = 14 L. Answer is option B.

mcqs.q: A mixture has sugar solution and water in 4 : 3. Adding 10 L of water makes it 4 : 5. Find the initial sugar solution.
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Let sugar = 4k, water = 3k. Step 2: 4k/(3k+10) = 4/5. Step 3: 20k = 12k + 40, so 8k = 40 and k = 5. Step 4: Sugar = 4 × 5 = 20 L. Answer is option B.

mcqs.q: Milk and water are in 5 : 3. Adding 6 L of water gives 5 : 4. Find the quantity of milk.
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Milk = 5k, water = 3k. Step 2: 5k/(3k+6) = 5/4. Step 3: 20k = 15k + 30, so k = 6. Step 4: Milk = 5 × 6 = 30 L. Answer is option C.

mcqs.q: Milk and water are in 5 : 2. Adding 10 L of water makes the ratio 5 : 3. Find the milk.
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Milk = 5k, water = 2k. Step 2: 5k/(2k+10) = 5/3. Step 3: 15k = 10k + 50, so 5k = 50 and k = 10. Step 4: Milk = 5 × 10 = 50 L. Answer is option C.

mcqs.q: A 60-litre mixture has milk : water = 2 : 1. How much water must be added to make it 8 : 5?
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Milk = 40 L, water = 20 L. Step 2: 40/(20+x) = 8/5. Step 3: 200 = 160 + 8x, so 8x = 40 and x = 5. Answer is option C.

mcqs.q: A 25-litre mixture has alcohol : water = 3 : 2. If 5 litres is removed and replaced by water, find the new ratio.
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Initially alcohol 15 L, water 10 L. Step 2: Remove 5 L of mixture: 3 L alcohol and 2 L water removed. Step 3: Left: alcohol 12 L, water 8 L. Step 4: Add 5 L water: water = 13 L. New ratio = 12 : 13. Answer is option A.

mcqs.q: A 45 kg alloy has copper : tin = 5 : 4. How much copper must be added so that the ratio becomes 10 : 7?
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Copper = 25 kg, tin = 20 kg. Step 2: (25+x)/20 = 10/7. Step 3: 7(25+x) = 200 → 175 + 7x = 200 → 7x = 25 → x = 25/7 kg. Answer is option A.

mcqs.q: A 35-litre mixture has milk : water = 4 : 3. How much water must be added to make it 2 : 3?
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Milk = 20 L, water = 15 L. Step 2: 20/(15+x) = 2/3. Step 3: 60 = 30 + 2x, so 2x = 30 and x = 15. Answer is option C.

mcqs.q: Vessel A has 80% milk, vessel B has 60% milk. They are mixed in 2 : 1. Find the milk percentage in the mixture.
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Milk in 2 parts A = 2 × 0.8 = 1.6 parts, in 1 part B = 0.6 parts. Step 2: Total milk = 2.2 out of 3 parts. Step 3: Percentage = (2.2/3) × 100 = 73.33%. Answer is option C.

mcqs.q: Milk and water are in 2 : 1. Adding 10 L of water makes the ratio 1 : 1. Find the milk.
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Milk = 2k, water = k. Step 2: 2k/(k+10) = 1/1. Step 3: 2k = k + 10, so k = 10. Step 4: Milk = 2 × 10 = 20 L. Answer is option B.

mcqs.q: An 8-litre mixture has milk : water = 5 : 3. Two litres is removed and replaced by milk. Find the new ratio.
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Initial milk 5 L, water 3 L. Step 2: Remove 2 L (ratio 5:3): milk 1.25 L, water 0.75 L removed. Step 3: Left: milk 3.75 L, water 2.25 L. Step 4: Add 2 L milk: milk 5.75 L. Ratio 5.75 : 2.25 = 23 : 9. Answer is option A.

mcqs.q: A 21-litre mixture has A : B = 4 : 3. How much B must be added to make it 2 : 3?
mcqs.exp: Step 1: A = 12 L, B = 9 L. Step 2: 12/(9+x) = 2/3. Step 3: 36 = 18 + 2x, so 2x = 18 and x = 9. Answer is option B.

mcqs.q: A 40-litre mixture has spirit : water = 17 : 3. How much water must be added to make it 17 : 5?
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Spirit = 34 L, water = 6 L. Step 2: 34/(6+x) = 17/5. Step 3: 170 = 102 + 17x, so 17x = 68 and x = 4. Answer is option B.

mcqs.q: Two vessels have milk : water = 2 : 3 and 5 : 1. They are mixed in 3 : 2. Find milk : water in the final mixture.
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Milk in 3 parts of A = 3 × (2/5) = 6/5. Milk in 2 parts of B = 2 × (5/6) = 5/3. Step 2: Total milk = 6/5 + 5/3 = (18+25)/15 = 43/15. Step 3: Total = 5 parts, water = 5 − 43/15 = 32/15. Step 4: Ratio = 43 : 32. Answer is option A.

mcqs.q: In what ratio must a 25% solution and a 50% solution be mixed to get a 40% solution?
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Alligation: 40 − 25 = 15 parts of the 50% solution, 50 − 40 = 10 parts of the 25% solution. Step 2: Ratio 25% : 50% = 10 : 15 = 2 : 3. Answer is option A.

mcqs.q: Incomes of P and Q are in 3 : 4. Each spends Rs 1000 and their savings are in 1 : 2. Find P's income.
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Let incomes be 3x and 4x. Savings = 3x−1000 and 4x−1000. Step 2: (3x−1000)/(4x−1000) = 1/2. Step 3: 6x − 2000 = 4x − 1000 → 2x = 1000 → x = 500. Step 4: P's income = 3 × 500 = Rs 1500. Answer is option B.

mcqs.q: Salaries of Ram and Sham are in 4 : 5. Each gets an increase of Rs 5000, making the ratio 50 : 60. Find Sham's present salary.
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Let salaries be 4x and 5x. Step 2: (4x+5000)/(5x+5000) = 50/60 = 5/6. Step 3: 6(4x+5000) = 5(5x+5000) → 24x + 30000 = 25x + 25000 → x = 5000. Step 4: Sham's present = 5 × 5000 + 5000 = Rs 30000. Answer is option B.

mcqs.q: A saves 30% of income, B saves 20%. Their savings are in 15 : 11. Find the ratio of their incomes.
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Income = saving ÷ saving rate. Step 2: A = 15/0.3 = 50, B = 11/0.2 = 55. Step 3: Ratio = 50 : 55 = 10 : 11. Answer is option A.

mcqs.q: Incomes of A and B are in 7 : 8. Each spends Rs 1000 and savings are in 3 : 4. Find A's income.
Salaries of A and B are in 5 : 6. Each gets an increase of Rs 3000, making the ratio 6 : 7. Find A's old salary.
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Salaries 5x, 6x. Step 2: (5x+3000)/(6x+3000) = 6/7. Step 3: 35x + 21000 = 36x + 18000 → x = 3000. Step 4: A's old = 5 × 3000 = Rs 15000. Answer is option B.

mcqs.q: Incomes of Ram and Sham are in 3 : 4. Each gets Rs 2000 more and the new ratio is 7 : 9. Find Sham's new salary.
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Incomes 3x, 4x. Step 2: (3x+2000)/(4x+2000) = 7/9. Step 3: 27x + 18000 = 28x + 14000 → x = 4000. Step 4: Sham new = 4 × 4000 + 2000 = Rs 18000. Answer is option B.

mcqs.q: P spends 80% of income, Q spends 85%. Their savings are in 8 : 9. Find the ratio of their incomes.
mcqs.exp: Step 1: P saves 20% → income = 8/0.2 = 40. Step 2: Q saves 15% → income = 9/0.15 = 60. Step 3: Ratio = 40 : 60 = 2 : 3. Answer is option A.

mcqs.q: A man, his wife and daughter worked 3, 2 and 4 days. Man : wife daily wage = 5 : 4 and man : daughter = 5 : 3. Total earnings Rs 105. Find the daughter's daily wage.
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Wages 5x, 4x, 3x. Step 2: 3(5x) + 2(4x) + 4(3x) = 105 → 15x + 8x + 12x = 35x = 105. Step 3: x = 3. Step 4: Daughter's wage = 3x = Rs 9. Answer is option A.

mcqs.q: Monthly incomes of A and B are in 5 : 4 and their expenditures in 7 : 5. Both save Rs 6000. Find A's income.
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Incomes 5x, 4x; expenditures 7y, 5y. Step 2: 5x − 7y = 6000 and 4x − 5y = 6000. Step 3: Subtract: x − 2y = 0 → x = 2y. Step 4: 4(2y) − 5y = 6000 → 3y = 6000 → y = 2000, x = 4000. Step 5: A's income = 5 × 4000 = Rs 20000. Answer is option C.

mcqs.q: Incomes of A and B are in 3 : 2 and expenditures in 5 : 3. Both save Rs 1000. Find B's income.
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Incomes 3x, 2x; expenditures 5y, 3y. Step 2: 3x − 5y = 1000 and 2x − 3y = 1000. Step 3: Subtract: x − 2y = 0 → x = 2y. Step 4: 3(2y) − 5y = 1000 → y = 1000, x = 2000. Step 5: B's income = 2 × 2000 = Rs 4000. Answer is option B.

mcqs.q: Incomes of X and Y are in 9 : 11 and their expenditures in 7 : 9. If each saves Rs 2000, find Y's income.
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Incomes 9x, 11x; expenditures 7y, 9y. Step 2: 9x − 7y = 2000 and 11x − 9y = 2000. Step 3: Subtract: 2x − 2y = 0 → x = y. Step 4: 9x − 7x = 2000 → 2x = 2000 → x = 1000. Step 5: Y's income = 11 × 1000 = Rs 11000. Answer is option B.

mcqs.q: A man spends 2/5 of his salary and saves the rest. If his savings are Rs 9000, find his salary.
mcqs.exp: Step 1: He saves 1 − 2/5 = 3/5 of salary. Step 2: (3/5) × Salary = 9000. Step 3: Salary = 9000 × 5/3 = Rs 15000. Answer is option C.

mcqs.q: A invests Rs 1,00,000 and B invests Rs 2,00,000 for the same period. Profit is Rs 30,000. Find A's share.
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Profit shares are in capital ratio 1 : 2. Step 2: Total parts = 3, one part = 30000/3 = 10000. Step 3: A's share = 1 × 10000 = Rs 10000. Answer is option A.

mcqs.q: A invests Rs 1000 for 6 months, B invests Rs 2000 for 3 months. Profit Rs 3000. Find B's share.
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Input = capital × time. A = 1000 × 6 = 6000, B = 2000 × 3 = 6000. Step 2: Ratio 1 : 1. Step 3: B's share = 3000/2 = Rs 1500. Answer is option B.

mcqs.q: A invests Rs 5000 for 8 months, B invests Rs 4000 for 6 months. Profit Rs 3200. Find A's share.

mcqs.q: 6 men can build a wall in 10 days. How many days will 15 men take?
mcqs.exp: Step 1: More men → fewer days (inverse proportion). Step 2: Total work = 6 × 10 = 60 man-days. Step 3: 15 men → 60/15 = 4 days. Answer is option B.

mcqs.q: 5 machines produce 200 toys. How many toys will 8 machines produce?
mcqs.exp: Step 1: More machines → more toys (direct proportion). Step 2: One machine = 200/5 = 40 toys. Step 3: 8 machines = 8 × 40 = 320. Answer is option C.

mcqs.q: x varies directly with y. If x = 12 when y = 3, find x when y = 7.
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Direct: x/y is constant = 12/3 = 4. Step 2: x = 4 × y. Step 3: x = 4 × 7 = 28. Answer is option C.

mcqs.q: x varies inversely with y. If x = 8 when y = 6, find x when y = 12.
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Inverse: x × y is constant = 8 × 6 = 48. Step 2: x = 48/12 = 4. Answer is option C.

mcqs.q: 12 pipes fill a tank in 8 hours. How long will 16 pipes take?
mcqs.exp: Step 1: More pipes → less time (inverse). Step 2: Total = 12 × 8 = 96 pipe-hours. Step 3: 16 pipes → 96/16 = 6 hours. Answer is option C.

mcqs.q: A car at 45 km/h takes 4 hours. At 60 km/h, how long will it take?
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Higher speed → less time (inverse). Step 2: Distance = 45 × 4 = 180 km. Step 3: Time = 180/60 = 3 hours. Answer is option B.

mcqs.q: 15 workers complete a job in 20 days. How many workers are needed for 12 days?
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Fewer days → more workers (inverse). Step 2: Work = 15 × 20 = 300 worker-days. Step 3: Workers = 300/12 = 25. Answer is option C.
